records.issue_text: Webhook endpoint findFirst-then-create/update is not atomic; concurrent webhook deliveries can create duplicate credentials for the same userId/appId
records.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), it does a read-then-write sequence: `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` and if not found it calls `prisma.credential.create(...)`. Two concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` can both observe “not found” and both attempt `create`, leading to duplicate credentials (if no unique constraint) or a uniqueness violation error (if a unique constraint exists). The diff does not show any unique constraint or an atomic `upsert` to prevent this race. | New webh

records.issue_text: Webhook secret comparison fails open if both header and configured secret are undefined, is not timing-safe, and uppercase characters in CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME cause all requests to 403 since Node lowercases header names
records.rationale:
In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check uses direct indexed header lookup and a normal string comparison:
```ts
req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET
```
Node/Next lowercases incoming header keys on `req.headers`, but the env-provided header name is not normalized in code, so a non-lowercase `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` will fail to match (case-sensitive property access). Also, comparing the shared secret with `!==` is not constant-time, which is a verifiable security weakness for secret
